title: Persistence-Driven Identity Exposure in Public Constructors
pattern: Forcing client-side creation or domain initialization routines to supply a surrogate, database-generated primary key (e.g., auto-increment `u64`) for new instances.
why_bad: It breaks core invariants. A newly created customer does not have a database identity yet. Requiring clients to supply a dummy value (e.g., `0` or `u64::MAX`) represents an invalid state and pollutes the domain with persistence mechanisms.
detection: Match public constructors (`pub fn new`) on entity structures requiring a surrogate primary key integer type (`u64`, `i64`, etc.) before any database record exists.
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 5, p. 203); *Domain-Driven Design* by Eric Evans (p. 25).
